item.content:encoded:
Yankees' playoff picture, Aaron Judge update and potential rotation
This wasn’t how the Yankees wanted to move into the regular season’s final week, with a four-game set against Tampa Bay.
Beginning with Tuesday’s day-night doubleheader, they’ll need to sweep the AL East leaders just to prevent the Rays from spilling champagne inside Yankee Stadium’s visiting clubhouse.
And there’s uncertainty surrounding Yankees captain Aaron Judge’s availability next week – the start of postseason − due to a right calf strain.
“We’ve been through a lot as a team this year already and we’ve answered the bell at mostly all the turns,’’ Yanks manager Aaron Boone told reporters, including the YES Network, after Sunday’s 8-4 loss at Arizona.
“(We’re) looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason.’’
Here’s a look at the Yankees’ week ahead:
Yankees vs Rays with AL East race nearing its end
In winning 12 of their last 15 games, the Rays (95-60) have opened a six-game divisional lead on the Yanks (89-66).
On the verge of its first AL East title since 2021, Tampa Bay could clinch it with one win on a long Tuesday in the Bronx.
Tuesday’s opener has Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) scheduled to oppose lefty Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95), with righty Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) vs. lefty Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the nightcap.
The Yanks are scheduled to start Gerrit Cole on Wednesday and Cam Schlittler on Thursday.
In the wider picture, Boone acknowledged the need to prep for next week, which includes giving important bullpen arms like Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn some added rest.
“You’ve got to make sure guys are in a good spot going in (to postseason),’’ Boone told reporters, speaking generally on Sunday.
“But we’re going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday.’’
Aaron Judge injury update
Judge’s availability for the first playoff round remains a mystery.
This past weekend, Judge told reporters: “I’d like to be back by the postseason. That’s definitely the plan.’’
Judge said he’s played through minor calf strains before, but this current injury to the soleus muscle is a more problematic spot.
So, this will be a key week of treatment and testing to see if Judge could be available in any capacity for a first-round playoff series.
Yankees injury news as Jazz Chisholm Jr. might return
Sidelined since Sept. 9, lefty-hitting second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (right thumb sprain) could be activated from the injured list to start the Tampa Bay series.
Though he’s unlikely to be activated this week, lefty reliever Ryan Weathers (flexor strain) could find himself on a playoff roster next week in a bullpen capacity.
On the IL since Sept. 5, center fielder Trent Grisham (strained right hamstring) has progressed in his running and is also a possible postseason choice.
Recovered from Tommy John surgery rehab, right-hander Clarke Schmidt developed cramping in his right biceps area while warming up Sunday.
Schmidt did not enter the game, telling reporters it was “more precautionary…especially with the playoffs coming up,’’ in what could be an important relief role.
Initial testing revealed no shoulder or elbow issues, but Schmidt planned to be examined by the team physician Monday.
Schmidt called it “frustrating,’’ but feels “in the grand scheme, we’ll be out there soon.’’
How Yankees' playoff rotation might look
With the likelihood of the Yanks hosting a best-of-three Wild Card series beginning Tuesday, they'd have Cam Schlittler ready on regular rest vs. Boston in Game 1.
But that might not be how the Yankees set things up.
Gerrit Cole would be on one extra day of rest if he's the Game 1 choice, or the Yanks could give the ball to Max Fried with nearly a full week of rest. It's been one month since Fried's return from a second elbow bone bruise this season.
Carlos Rodon could be on a Wild Card roster in an emergency or long relief capacity, or he might be saved to start Game 1 or 2 of a best-of-five Division Series.
CC Sabathia to be honored at Yankee Stadium
Prior to Saturday night's game against the Orioles, CC Sabathia's No. 52 will be retired in a ceremony at Yankee Stadium.
He'll be the 24th Yankees player or manager so honored and the first since Paul O'Neill, who had his No. 21 retired in August 2022.

item.title: [amazinavenue.com] Monday Stat Party: Put him in the books
item.dc:creator: Linus Lawrence
item.description: Welcome back to Monday Stat Party, a weekly series showcasing some of the most curious and nostalgia-inducing statistical developments from the past week of Mets baseball. What unites each entry is the sense of intrigue which they aim to spark, and the unbridled love of the game’s anomalies from which they arise. Without further ado, let the stat party begin. MONDAY A.J. Ewing hit his 10th home run of the season, giving the Mets 11 players with 10+ homers and setting a new record for most 10-hom
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Monday Stat Party, a weekly series showcasing some of the most curious and nostalgia-inducing statistical developments from the past week of Mets baseball. What unites each entry is the sense of intrigue which they aim to spark, and the unbridled love of the game’s anomalies from which they arise. Without further ado, let the stat party begin.
MONDAY
A.J. Ewing hit his 10th home run of the season, giving the Mets 11 players with 10+ homers and setting a new record for most 10-homer players in a season in franchise history (the 2017 team previously held the record with 10 10-homer players). They are now tied for the fifth-most 10-homer players on a team in baseball history, behind the 2019 Yankees (14), 2019 Blue Jays (13), 2018 Yankees (12), and 2023 Twins (12).
TUESDAY
Pete Alonso became the 20th player to record their 300th homer against a team for which they previously played, and the third to do so against a team for which they played 1,000 or more games (along with Willie Horton against the Tigers and Torii Hunter against the Twins). (source: Sarah Langs on X, per Elias Sports Bureau)
Alonso became the second player to hit their 300th homer at Citi Field, as Curtis Granderson reached the milestone with a go-ahead homer in the eighth inning on June 14, 2017, against the Cubs.
The homer marked Alonso’s first game-tying or go-ahead home run while trailing in the ninth inning or later since Game 3 of the 2024 Wild Card Series.
Alonso was actually the second former Met to hit a game-tying or go-ahead home run at Citi Field while trailing in the ninth inning or later. It may not have received the same fanfare as the Polar Bear’s blast, but Adeiny Hecchavarría accomplished the feat with the Braves off Paul Sewald on September 29, 2019 — exactly one day after Alonso set a new MLB rookie record with his 53rd home run of the season. Hechavarría’s homer set up Dom Smith’s memorable walk-off homer on the final pitch of the regular season.
Alonso’s homer snapped Kodai Senga’s streak of seven consecutive saves successfully converted, the fourth-most by a Met to begin their career behind Tug McGraw (15), Anthony Young (12), and Hisanori Takahashi (8).
A.J. Ewing’s second-inning single marked the 100th hit of his career. Ewing and Carson Benge are just the third pair of Mets rookies to record 100 hits in the same season, joining Steve Henderson and Lee Mazzilli in 1977 and Jason Phillips and Ty Wigginton in 2003.
Since 2015, there have been four extra-inning inside-the-park homers in MLB. Three of those four have been hit by an opposing player at Citi Field: Blake Swihart of the Red Sox on August 28, 2015, Daylen Lile of the Nationals on September 20, 2025, and now Coby Mayo of the Orioles on September 15, 2026. The only other extra-inning inside-the-park homer in that span was hit by another Oriole, Austin Hays, on August 11, 2020, at Citizens Bank Park.
Mayo’s inside-the-park homer was a wind-prevented traditional homer, marking the first time a wind-prevented traditional homer has resulted in an inside-the-parker since…Daylen Lile’s on September 20, 2025, at Citi Field. (source: Sarah Langs on X, per Weather Applied Metrics)
The Mets played their 18th extra-inning game of the season, marking the fourth-most in the majors behind the Angels (20), Cubs (19) and Cardinals (19). It’s the most extra-inning games the Mets have played in a season since 2018 (18).
WEDNESDAY
With his 24th stolen base of the season, A.J. Ewing tied Mookie Wilson’s 1981 record for the most stolen bases by a rookie in franchise history.
By allowing homers to Pete Alonso, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, and Jeremiah Jackson, the Mets allowed homers to the same three players in back-to-back games for the first time in franchise history.
The Orioles hit three homers at 106+ mph against the Mets for the second day in a row. Prior to this series, the Mets hadn’t allowed three such homers in a game since April 4, 2023, during a 9-0 loss in Milwaukee.
Chris Bassitt completed six innings at Citi Field for the 16th time since 2022. He is tied with David Peterson for the most six-inning outings at Citi Field during that span, despite the fact that Bassitt played just one season as a Met.
Alonso hit his 125th homer at Citi Field. No other player has more than 80 (Francisco Lindor). It was also Alonso’s 58th homer of a Statcast-projected 410+ feet at Citi Field. No other player has more than 23 (Michael Conforto).
The Mets have now lost five games in a row against the Orioles, and nine of their last 12.
THURSDAY
Nolan McLean has a 0.71 ERA over his first four career starts against the Phillies. That’s tied with Chuck Taylor for the fourth-lowest ERA in a pitcher’s first four starts against the Phillies since the mound was lowered in 1969 (min. 20 IP), behind Rick Honeycutt (0.38), Bob Sykes (0.42), and Hiroki Kuroda (0.68).
McLean recorded his 19th quality start this season, tied with Sonny Gray and Chris Sale for sixth-most in the majors behind Sandy Alcantara (21), Yoshinobu Yamamoto (21), Cristopher Sánchez (21), Cam Schlittler (20), and Michael Wacha (20). McLean is one of only two pitchers since 2015 to reach 19 quality starts in their rookie season, joining Shota Imanaga (19 in 2024). McLean also recorded his 20th start of six or more innings pitched this season, the second-most by a Met in a season since 2020, trailing only Wednesday’s opposing starter: Chris Bassitt (23 in 2022).
McLean recorded his 25th game with at least five strikeouts this season, the most by a Mets pitcher since Jacob deGrom (29) and Noah Syndergaard (27) in 2019.
Aaron Nola made his 33rd career start against the Mets, tied for 25th all-time against the franchise and tied with Randy Wolf and Tim Hudson for second-most since 2000, behind fellow longtime Phillies pitcher Cole Hamels (34). It was his 16th start as a visiting player at Citi Field, moving him into second place behind Gio Gonzalez (18) for most opposing starts in the ballpark’s history.
Nola recorded his seventh scoreless start against the Mets, tying him for the sixth-most all-time behind Rick Reuschel (11), Greg Maddux (10), Juan Marichal (9), Claude Osteen (9), and Jim Bunning (8).
The Mets suffered their 15th shutout loss of the season, tied with the Angels, Guardians, and Pirates for the second-most in MLB behind the Reds (17).
FRIDAY
Juan Soto reached base three times for the 324th time in his career, tying Mike Trout for the fourth-most such games by a player before turning 28 years old. Soto trails only Jimmie Foxx (348), Mickey Mantle (344), and Mel Ott (341).
Soto ripped two extra-base hits with an exit velocity of 108 mph or higher in the same game. In the statcast era (since 2015), a Mets left-handed hitter has accomplished that feat only 12 times: Robinson Cano, Lucas Duda, and Daniel Vogelbach each did it once, Brandon Nimmo did it twice, Michael Conforto did it three times, and Juan Soto has now done it four times in just two seasons.
Zac Thornton recorded his eighth quality start through 14 career games, marking the third-most by a Mets left-handed pitcher behind Steven Matz (10) and Sid Fernandez (9).
SATURDAY
Carson Benge’s eighth-inning single marked his 156th hit of the season, passing Pete Alonso to set the franchise’s new rookie hits record.
Benge recorded his 12th three-hit game of the season, marking another record for a Mets rookie, while notching three hits and a homer against the Phillies. The Mets outfielder with the most such games against the Phillies? Carlos Beltrán (7 times), who had his number retired in a pregame ceremony on Saturday.
The Mets scored 10 or more runs for the 18th time this season, tied with 1997 for the third-most such games in a season in franchise history. The 2000 (24) and 1999 (20) teams are the only ones in franchise history with more double-digit scoring performances.
SUNDAY
Francisco Alvarez’s second-inning single was his 23rd batted ball at 108 mph or higher this season, tied with Juan Soto for the most on the team.
The Mets scored two or fewer runs through nine innings for the 62nd time this season. That’s the most such games for the Mets in a season since 2013 (63), and their second-most in the Wild Card Era (since 1995).
The Mets finished the season with a losing record (3-4) against the Phillies at Citi Field for the first time since 2019, when they went 4-5.
The Mets finished the season with a 36-45 record at Citi Field, their worst in a full season since 2013, when they went 33-48.
Miscellaneous Mets stat of the week:
Here is a list of every player to record 99+ homers and 99+ stolen bases with multiple franchises:
Barry Bonds (Pirates and Giants)
Alex Rodriguez (Mariners and Yankees)
Carlos Beltrán (Royals and Mets)
Francisco Lindor (Guardians and Mets)
Beltrán’s 70.0 career bWAR ranks second all-time among players born in Puerto Rico, trailing only that of Roberto Clemente (95.0). Beltrán won the Roberto Clemente Award in 2013, and Francisco Lindor (who ranks fifth on the leaderboard with 57.2 bWAR) was named the Mets’ 2026 nominee last Monday.
Bonus Stat: There are 32 entries in this edition of Monday Stat Party — one for each year of Mets baseball that Howie Rose has called from the broadcast booth.

item.title: [azsnakepit.com] Pave Ruth
item.dc:creator: Joshua Hunt
item.description: A gut punching series loss at the hands of the Miami Marlins not only had the Diamondbacks lose more ground in the NL Wild Card race to the 3 teams ahead of them, it also seemed to take all the hopium that remained in our systems and replace it with either copium or just straight up despair as the D’Backs would go from 2 losing series against 2 sub .500 teams to welcoming the New York Yankees into town for the final home series of the 2026 season. The Yankees may have already secured their spot
item.content:encoded:
A gut punching series loss at the hands of the Miami Marlins not only had the Diamondbacks lose more ground in the NL Wild Card race to the 3 teams ahead of them, it also seemed to take all the hopium that remained in our systems and replace it with either copium or just straight up despair as the D’Backs would go from 2 losing series against 2 sub .500 teams to welcoming the New York Yankees into town for the final home series of the 2026 season.
The Yankees may have already secured their spot in October before their trip to the desert but with a chance at the AL East title still a possibility, along with having Gerrit Cole and the probable AL Cy Young winner in Cam Schlittler taking the bump, this would be no cake walk of a series and the Diamondbacks would need to at least win this series if they want any sliver of hope going into their final 6 games in Colorado and San Diego. With the 25th anniversary of the 2001 World Series winning team being celebrated this series, maybe they would be able to have some of that magic rub off onto this 2026 ballclub and use it as the fuel they need to propel them towards postseason baseball.
Ed-Rough-do Start-Riguez
Eduardo Rodriguez has undoubtedly been the best starter in the Diamondbacks rotation for all of 2026 as he leads the starters in wins (15), ERA (2.89), IP (183.2) and K’s (140), but the issue that has been rearing its head all season for Rodriguez has been his struggles out of the gate and we got more of the same in Friday night’s series opener with the Yankees putting up a 5 spot before the Diamondbacks even had the chance to swing the lumber.
The three of us looked at ERod’s numbers from the 1st inning of his starts compared to the rest of the game and it was as night and day as it could get with his first inning ERA this season sitting at 7.84, a WHIP of 1.77 and an opposing slash of .302/.389/579. From the 2nd inning and beyond he evolves into a completely different pitcher with his 1.89 ERA, 1.12 WHIP and opposing hitter slashing just .222/.279/.326. This isn’t even necessarily just an issue he’s had in 2026 either as his career ERA in the 1st inning (4.51) compared to the rest of his innings (3.92) shows that he’s always had struggles early in games for most of his career.
Cravin for Pavin?
With the demoralizing 9-2 loss on Friday night the Diamondbacks and all snakes fans in attendance would hope that the vibes would be turned around as Saturday would be the big 25th anniversary celebration of the greatest world series of all time (yes I’m biased) with so many legends from that squad like Randy Johnson, Luis Gonzalez, Tony Womack, Miguel Batista, Damien Miller and more in the building for the festivities.
Both the Yankees and Diamondbacks had clutch pitching and hitting at times throughout this game as the score was knotted at 3 a piece going into the bottom of the 9th inning with the Snakes in desperate need of a win to keep their playoff hopes from lowering even further, and that’s when the infamous Pavin Smith stepped in the box as a pinch hitter with a runner on 1st and 1 out. The baseball gods must like reruns because they decided that a Diamondbacks walk-off of the Yankees on the night of the 2001 WS celebration would be the most fitting outcome, and Pavin delivered just that with a 2-R home run into the sea of Yankee fans in right field.
All 3 of us have been very vocal in our frustrations with Smith’s struggles in his career here in the desert and the front office seeming to refuse to move on from a player that has accumulated 0.1 bWAR in his time as a major leaguer, and we all still feel that he should not be on this roster at the beginning of the 2027 season (if we have one that is) in any capacity, but we did admit that it was nice to see Pavin summon his inner Luis Gonzalez and send the fans into a frenzy with a walk-off over the Yankees.
Unc-enado Still Got It
The fireworks might have been after the game on Friday night, but Sunday’s final home game of the 2026 regular season had plenty of leftovers as it felt like baseballs were flying out left and right. Most of them came for the Yankees off of Corbin Burnes in the 4th inning, but the biggest one was in the Diamondbacks favor with Nolan Arenado hitting a go ahead (and potential season saving) grand slam in the 5th inning, his 3rd in 2026 and the 9th of his career.
The fellas and I discussed how nice of a surprise this offensive resurgence has been from Arenado as he is putting up some of the best numbers at the dish we have seen since his MVP caliber season as a Cardinal in 2022 while also pondering the likelihood that Nolan can get to 30 home runs on the season (27 currently) with 3 of the final 6 games being played in his old stomping grounds of Coors Field where Arenado has 139 dingers in his career in the mile high city.
Colorado Cookin
Setting off for the final road trip of the regular season the Snakes will be heading to Coors Field to take on the Colorado Rockies as they continue to battle for their lives in an attempt to make miracles happen and sneak into the playoffs.
The last few weeks have seen us and other fans throw the term “must-win games” around a bunch but these 3 in Colorado are all truly must win games if the Diamondbacks want to have any real chance at making the final series in San Diego mean anything as a Diamondbacks loss+Padres win, 2 D’Backs losses or 2 Padres wins would put the final nail in the coffin of the Diamondbacks playoff hopes.
Gabe, Brandon and I all felt disgusted that we would have to actually root for the Los Angeles Dodgers to win baseball games (just typing that out makes me want to puke) but that is the reality we are in as a Dodgers sweep of the Padres with the Diamondbacks sweeping the Rockies would set us up for what could most likely feel like its own wild card series against the Padres in San Diego to decide who gets in and who goes to Cancun.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Why the Yankees can overcome concerning Aaron Judge development in the MLB playoffs

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge’s latest injury has created another major question for the New York Yankees heading into the MLB playoffs.
Judge landed on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a right calf strain after returning from a lengthy absence earlier this month. The Yankees have not provided a timetable for his return, leaving his availability for October unclear.
There is no replacing Judge’s presence in the lineup. Still, New York has one major reason to believe it can survive without its captain: a starting rotation capable of controlling games in October.
Yankees can lean on their starting rotation
The Yankees’ pitching staff has given the team a foundation strong enough to withstand another stretch without Judge.
Cam Schlittler has emerged as the biggest reason for that confidence. The second-year right-hander entered his final regular-season starts with a 14-6 record and a 1.95 ERA, establishing himself as the Yankees’ top postseason pitching option.
Max Fried has also been excellent, carrying a 2.63 ERA through 19 starts. Gerrit Cole has provided another experienced arm with a 3.63 ERA and 123 strikeouts in 21 starts.
Carlos Rodón gives New York another left-handed option. He has also pitched well since returning from his elbow injury, allowing two runs over six innings in his most recent start against Minnesota.
That combination matters in the postseason. If the Yankees can consistently get quality starts, they do not need their offense to produce at the same level every night.
Mark DeRosa sees a path without Judge
MLB Network analyst Mark DeRosa made a similar point when discussing Judge’s injury and the Yankees’ postseason outlook.
“Concern level for Aaron Judge’s injury and the Yankees? Can they overcome it? Yes. They’re built on the strength of their starting rotation,” DeRosa said.
DeRosa also acknowledged the obvious issue. The Yankees need Judge’s presence in the lineup when October arrives, but their pitching gives them another way to win games.
That was already evident during Judge’s earlier absence. He missed more than three months with a rib injury, yet New York still reached the postseason.
The Yankees have already secured a playoff spot, but they still have important games remaining against Tampa Bay. Their final week will help determine their postseason position.
Judge’s return would obviously change the Yankees’ ceiling. But if he cannot make it back in time, New York has something many teams would want in October: multiple starting pitchers capable of taking control of a playoff game.
For the Yankees, that could be the difference between simply surviving Judge’s absence and remaining a serious postseason threat.

item.title: [windfm.com] Justin Verlander is retiring. With a work stoppage on the horizon, how many others might join him? - WINDFM - 92.5 Gainesville 95.5 Ocala
item.dc:creator: Schristian
item.description: By NOAH TRISTER AP Baseball Writer Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer were together on some memorable Detroit teams before moving on and winning championships elsewhere. Will they eventually enter the Hall of Fame as part of the same class? The first question is whether both will retire after this season. item.content:encoded:
By NOAH TRISTER AP Baseball Writer
Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer were together on some memorable Detroit teams before moving on and winning championships elsewhere.
Will they eventually enter the Hall of Fame as part of the same class?
The first question is whether both will retire after this season. The 43-year-old Verlander has already announced this is his final year. He’s made only one start in a reunion season with the Tigers, although Detroit fans are hoping he can return for another this coming week.
Scherzer’s future is less clear. The 42-year-old right-hander is slated to start Tuesday at Baltimore as the Blue Jays try to keep their flickering playoff hopes alive, but Scherzer has posted ERAs over 5.00 both this season and last. He’s on a one-year contract with Toronto.
Some other prominent players may also have made — or might be making — their last appearances in the major leagues. Trey Mancini signed a one-day contract to retire with the Orioles and was celebrated this past weekend in Baltimore. Andrew McCutchen and Carlos Santana, both 39, were released last month. Craig Kimbrel, now 38, has pitched for 10 different big league teams in the last six seasons.
Paul Goldschmidt is 39, but his team — the New York Yankees — is heading to the playoffs. And he may be more important than expected if Aaron Judge is out.
With a lockout possible after this season, there could be some retirements we don’t anticipate. Rick Sutcliffe, Bo Jackson and Hall of Famer Goose Gossage, for example, never played again after the 1994 strike but didn’t actually retire until the following year.
Trivia time
Who is the most recent player voted into the Hall of Fame by the BBWAA whose primary team was the Tigers? (The drought is likely to end soon with Miguel Cabrera and then Verlander.)
Performance of the week
Angel Martínez homered from both sides of the plate and had four hits in Cleveland’s 12-6 win over the Athletics on Saturday night. The Guardians have won five straight and are closing in on a postseason spot. They have a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox atop the AL Central, and it’s another three games back from the White Sox to Toronto and Houston in the race for the last wild card.
In the National League, Philadelphia leads Arizona by four games for the final wild card, so anyone rooting for chaos this coming week may be disappointed.
Comeback of the week
Detroit was down 8-2 in the fifth inning Friday night before scoring nine unanswered runs to win 11-8 over the White Sox. Kevin McGonigle hit a three-run triple, and both Hao-Yu Lee and Riley Greene added two-run homers during the comeback. Detroit’s win probability was down to 3.2% in the fourth inning according to Baseball Savant.
That’s the only game the Tigers have won out of their last five. They’ve been eliminated from the playoff race, the end of a frustrating season in which nothing seemed to go as planned.
Team of the week
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres both went 6-1, with the Dodgers posting the superior run differential. A three-game sweep of San Francisco leaves the Dodgers four games ahead of Atlanta for the second bye in the National League as they try for a third consecutive World Series title.
There are still health concerns for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Blake Snell having left his last start after one inning.
Los Angeles did get Edwin Diaz back, and he threw scoreless innings on back-to-back days Friday and Saturday.
Trivia answer
Al Kaline, who was inducted in 1980.
George Kell, Hal Newhouser, Jim Bunning, Sparky Anderson, Jack Morris and Alan Trammell have been elected since then with the Tigers as their primary team, but they weren’t voted in by the BBWAA.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here

item.title: [cronkitenews.azpbs.org] The legacy of the Diamondbacks’ 2001 World Series title
item.dc:creator: Logan Heath
item.description: PHOENIX – Hours before the 2001 Arizona Diamondbacks made a memorable homecoming, Curt Schilling stood on the mound he once ruled, this time with his 1-year-old grandson Nolan, named after Schilling’s pitching idol. item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX – Hours before the 2001 Arizona Diamondbacks made a memorable homecoming, Curt Schilling stood on the mound he once ruled, this time with his 1-year-old grandson Nolan, named after Schilling’s pitching idol.
Schilling gently helped Nolan mimic throwing a pitch, maybe one of those splitters that once devastated hitters. It was a heartwarming snapshot of the future and the past, a moment that captured the ceremonies Saturday at Chase Field.
As the former players, older and grayer, took in the festivities with their families, dressed in throwback purple jerseys, Schilling looked around at the ballpark where magic once happened and predicted, somewhat hopefully, that the grandson named after Nolan Ryan was going to be “a right-handed, mid-90s guy and a left-shot defenseman.”
It was a full circle moment on a day that had many.
On Saturday, the 2001 Diamondbacks returned to Chase Field to celebrate the 25th anniversary of their improbable World Series victory over the New York Yankees. The team was greeted with long and well-deserved applause as the players made their way down a red carpet rolled out for them.
Chase Field, once Bank One Ballpark, is a place where the Diamondbacks have always felt welcome, but 25 years ago, it was one of the few places they felt the love.
“Usually nobody outside of New York roots for the Yankees,” said Schilling, who shared MVP honors with fellow pitcher Randy Johnson in that series. “But it was different after 9/11, and we understood that.”
In the wake of terrorist attacks that brought down the World Trade Center’s north and south towers on Sept. 11, 2001, the country was rallying around the city of New York and the three-time defending champion Yankees.
That was the backdrop against which the Diamondbacks chased their first title in just their fourth season of existence. But that series was about much more than the upstart Diamondbacks, who had joined the NL as an expansion team in 1998, or the Yankees, who were hoping to extend their dynasty.
Both teams were playing in a country still trying to make sense of the attacks. But as emotional as the circumstances surrounding the attacks were, the players still had a World Series to play.
“It was very emotional knowing everything New York had been through,” said David Dellucci, an outfielder on that 2001 team who attended the celebration. “We went to Ground Zero. We visited first responders and families who lost loved ones in the attacks. So our hearts went out to all of them.”
Schilling emphasized the impact the attacks had on the national mood.
“I think we became a lot closer as a country during that time,” Schilling said. “We were very united and patriotic.”
The Yankees had faced a great deal of adversity on their journey to the World Series that year. In the five-game ALDS they overcame a 2-0 deficit against the Oakland Athletics and went on to beat the Seattle Mariners – a team that had won 116 games during the 2001 regular season – in the ALCS.
The Diamondbacks, meanwhile, won the NL West, beat St. Louis in a division series and defeated Atlanta for the NL pennant to reach the World Series faster than any expansion team in history.
In any other circumstance, the Diamondbacks might have been the sentimental favorite.
“Even the players were torn because we knew how important it was,” Dellucci said. “But it was our job to go out there and play hard and try our best to win it.”
With the country watching and the weight of everything that had happened just weeks earlier still fresh in everybody’s minds, the Diamondbacks and Yankees took the field in a thrilling seven-game series.
Although the Yankees were three-time defending champions, the Diamondbacks were not intimidated.
“None of that stuff mattered to us,” Schilling said. “We were playing for a championship. We had a group of guys who had been around a long time and wanted to win.”
Arizona dominated the first two games played at Bank One Ballpark. They beat the Yankees 9-1 and 4-0 with Schilling and Johnson as the winning pitchers.
Then the series moved to New York, where President George W. Bush, wearing a bullet-proof vest under his jacket, threw out the first pitch before an emotional Game 3 at Yankee Stadium.
The Yankees won the next three, all one-run games and with two going to extra innings. However, with another blowout win – this time 15-2 – in Game 6, the Diamondbacks forced a Game 7.
It turned out to be one of the most memorable games in baseball history.
Schilling started on the mound and kept the Diamondbacks in the game, but the Yankees took a 2-1 lead in the eighth on an Alfonso Soriano homer, putting Arizona’s chance of winning a championship on the ropes.
Johnson, who shared series MVP honors with Schilling, started and went seven innings to win Game 6. Then he dramatically came out of the bullpen with the Diamondbacks trailing 2-1 to get the last out in the top of the eight inning and pitch a scoreless top of the ninth, setting the stage for Arizona’s bottom-of-the-ninth heroics against Yankees closer Mariano Rivera.
During Saturday’s celebration, as the Diamondbacks gathered on the mound, Johnson fittingly entered out of the bullpen in left field carrying the World Series trophy. It was one of several special touches for a day celebrating the Valley’s only major pro sports title by a men’s team.
Even when the script didn’t go according to plan on Saturday, the performers improvised beautifully.
Later, Johnson recalled what the Diamondbacks were up against in that final inning.
“I remember walking off the mound after pitching the top of the ninth while we were still losing 2-1,” Johnson said. “I knew what Mariano Rivera had done in his regular and postseason career, so I knew it was going to be an uphill battle.”
The Diamondbacks had three outs to work with against Rivera, who had been all but unhittable. He entered that game with 23 consecutive postseason saves.
But Arizona rallied for two runs in the bottom of the ninth, capped by Luis Gonzalez’s dramatic walk-off flare single that drove in Jay Bell for the winning run and completed the comeback.
For the players in the dugout, it was almost impossible to process the victory. They were moments away from losing the World Series and now they were rushing the field to celebrate a championship.
“I just watched everything unfold in the dugout,” Johnson said. “It went from not knowing if we were going to win to dogpiling on the mound. And from that point on, until the next month or so, everything was just surreal.”
For Dellucci, the Game 7 victory was everything for which he could have asked.
“As a kid, that’s what you always dream about is winning a World Series,” he said. “And we were able to do it that night, and not only get it done with our best friends and closest teammates, but also in front of our home fans.”
Even now, 25 years later, the 2001 World Series is remembered as one of the greatest in the sport’s history.
“There is no chance it’s not in the top two or three best of all time,” Schilling said. “I think if you go back and look at this series as a non-Yankee fan, it all happened perfectly. They won all three games in New York. Three amazing games. We had the Game 7 walk-off win and all the drama and emotion that came with it.”
A quarter of a century later, the legacy of that Arizona club lives on and the memories still remain fresh in the minds of the players.
“Twenty-five years goes by pretty quick,” Johnson said. “But it would be fun to do this again in 25 years or maybe sooner. The 2023 team came pretty close to winning another, but hopefully they’ll come close again and we can celebrate a newer one soon.”
The 2001 Diamondbacks’ World Series victory remains a defining moment in Arizona sports history, a victory shared by a team, a city and a country during an unforgettable time.
In a fitting crescendo to the 25-year celebration, the Series co-MVPs met in the infield to hoist the trophy once more.
They nearly sealed the moment with a kiss.

item.content:encoded:
Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s return from a right thumb sprain is near, meaning the Yankees face some interesting decisions.
The second baseman could be activated from the injured list as soon as Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Rays, and while the corresponding roster move appears simple (Max Schuemann), the potential lineup moves bear watching.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
After Chisholm got hurt diving into second base Sept. 8, the Yankees called up Anthony Volpe to get some run at the position he had mostly transitioned to at Triple-A, and he made the most of it.
In the 10 games since Volpe was recalled, he has started at second base nine times (José Caballero started the other) and mostly looked sharp, batting .286 with a .753 OPS and four steals.
Whether Volpe has done enough to warrant at-bats once Chisholm returns remains to be seen. Shortly before he was called back up, the natural shortstop had also started to mix in some third base, starting three games there, though Aaron Boone would only offer, “We’ll see,” when asked whether that could be an option for Volpe with Chisholm back.
“First things first, getting Jazz back and then we’ll figure it out as the week unfolds how I want to play it,” Boone said.
The Yankees have not gotten much offensive production from their third basemen this year, especially of late. Since returning from his own thumb sprain Sept. 1, Ryan McMahon has hit just 6-for-40 (.150) with a .402 OPS, with Caballero starting at third over him Sunday against a righty. Amed Rosario has often started at third against lefties, and while he has not hit in line with his career numbers, the Yankees continue to believe he will.
Boone could also platoon Volpe and Chisholm at second base, as the lefty-hitting Chisholm is batting only .221 with a .654 OPS against lefties. But the pending free agent had just been starting to get hot in a disappointing season, hitting .391 with a 1.028 OPS over his last 15 games before getting hurt.
If and where Volpe fits on the playoff roster is just one of the many decisions they will have to consider over this final week of the regular season.
“You know it’s going to take a lot of players and a lot of people when you get to spring training and the season unfolds,” Boone said. “We’ll have hopefully some tough decisions to make when we’re setting postseason rosters and things like that. But that’s a better problem to have.”
Shop Yankees Merch
Clarke Schmidt was expected to see the team doctor early this week after experiencing biceps cramping while warming up Sunday, which kept him from entering the game. The right-hander had just made his return from Tommy John surgery and is trying to carve out a role in the playoff bullpen.
Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain) could also have a role in a playoff bullpen, but first the lefty will need to face hitters this week as he tries to show the Yankees he could jump right into postseason action without pitching in a game since he got hurt Aug. 22.

item.dc:creator: Jose Rodriguez
item.description: - MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie” - MLB. Aaron Judge desata la preocupación tras abandonar el juego por una lesión repentina días después de volver a MLB Los New York Yankees recibieron otro duro golpe en la recta final de la temporada después de verse obligados a colocar nuevamente a Aaron Judge en la lista de lesionados (IL), apenas una semana después de su regreso tras una fractura en las costillas que lo mantuvo fuera du
item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani: “Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”
- MLB. Aaron Judge desata la preocupación tras abandonar el juego por una lesión repentina días después de volver a MLB
Los New York Yankees recibieron otro duro golpe en la recta final de la temporada después de verse obligados a colocar nuevamente a Aaron Judge en la lista de lesionados (IL), apenas una semana después de su regreso tras una fractura en las costillas que lo mantuvo fuera durante 60 días.
El capitán de los Yankees ahora enfrenta una distensión en la pantorrilla. Aunque es elegible para volver cuando solamente resten un par de partidos de temporada regular, todavía existe incertidumbre sobre si el equipo decidirá activarlo.
Con Nueva York ya clasificado a la postemporada, la organización enfrenta una decisión clave en los próximos días: arriesgar el regreso de su máxima estrella o darle más tiempo de recuperación pensando en los playoffs.
Aaron Judge podría no volver a jugar esta temporada
El panorama, sin embargo, no luce alentador. El periodista Joel Sherman, de The New York Post, considera que existe una posibilidad real de que Judge no vuelva a disputar un partido este año, incluso si los Yankees avanzan lejos en la postemporada.
“Existe una posibilidad bastante fuerte de que Aaron Judge no vuelva a jugar esta temporada”, aseguró Sherman recientemente.
Aunque las palabras del reportero no representan una confirmación definitiva, sí funcionan como una señal de alerta para los Yankees, quienes podrían llegar a octubre sin su principal referente ofensivo.
La parte positiva para Nueva York es que el equipo ya pasó gran parte de la temporada adaptándose a jugar sin su estrella. Aunque las aspiraciones de Serie Mundial reciben un duro golpe sin Judge en la alineación, el roster ha demostrado que puede competir incluso sin su capitán.
¿Qué dijo Aaron Judge sobre su lesión?
El capitán de los Yankees no ocultó su frustración después de regresar nuevamente a la lista de lesionados el sábado. Aunque evitó dar detalles sobre la gravedad de su distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, Judge dejó claro que mantiene la esperanza de estar disponible para la postemporada.
“Me gustaría estar de regreso para los playoffs. Ese es definitivamente el plan. Es la lista de lesionados de 10 días, así que el décimo día probablemente sea el último partido de la temporada regular. Ya veremos. Realmente no tengo respuestas sobre algún calendario o algo por el estilo”, explicó Judge.

item.content:encoded:
Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. I dig into the top adds on the ever-popular Fantrax and in the NFBC Online Championship (OC), a national mid-stakes contest with 240 total leagues of 12 and a six-figure grand prize. Reviewing player adds between the two should provide us with a well-rounded perspective and barometer of the fantasy baseball marketplace.
Week 26 Overview
Hitters
The San Diego Padres took advantage of their four-game series with the Rockies at Coors Field and a home set with the Marlins, scoring 51 runs, 12 more than any other team. Fernando Tatis Jr. (along with Brandon Lowe and Pete Crow-Armstrong) led the way with a week-high four dingers. Last week’s streamers turned out to be dynamite: Jake Cronenworth (.464-8-2-8-2), Dustin Harris (.379-5-0-7-2) and Samad Taylor (.556-6-1-7-1) really stepped up, particularly Taylor for my competitive Main Event squad that gained two category points in batting average last week. Rake Cronenworth was true to his nickname from several years ago. He led all Major League hitters with 13 hits. The Brewers swiped a league-high 12 bags last week: four each for Jackson Chourio and rookie Cooper Pratt. Tampa’s Chandler Simpson led all runners with five swipes, finally catching Washington’s Nasim Nuñez for the MLB lead with 46. Expect Simpson to finish with 50+ and win the stolen base crown.
Pitchers
Of the 29 two-start pitchers excluding Pirates opener Lake Bachar, three earned two wins: Tarik Skubal, Sean Burke and David Peterson. Houston’s Hunter Brown had an outstanding two-step (10 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 5 K – 20 K) and those 20 punchouts led all pitchers for the week. Gavin Williams punched out 16 in 12 innings and is back atop the AL lead in strikeouts with 244. Dylan Cease (239) may not make his final start of the season and Cam Schlittler (234) is unlikely to catch Williams as both have one start remaining. It’s very possible that Williams catches and passes Jacob Misiorowski (247) for the Major League lead. The Miz pitched three innings in his weekend start and might be limited for his final one.
Tampa’s Bryan Baker was the first reliever to reach 40 saves this season. It’s possible that Cade Smith (39), Riley O’Brien (38) and Mason Miller (37) join Baker. The last time there were three closers with 40 or more saves was in 2019: Edwin Díaz (57), Wade Davis (43), and Craig Kimbrel (42). Shout out to folks who drafted O’Brien late, and/or picked up Baker, Louis Varland or Jacob Latz off waivers and didn’t have to worry about the saves category all season.
Week 27 Most Added Players: NFBC Main Event, NFBC OC, and Fantrax
It’s the last hurrah for managers with FAB dollars left, hoping to get the best bang for the buck and for variance to lean their way and tip them into league titles. As is usually the case in the final week, we hope to optimize our pitching rotations and hitters in hitter-friendly ballparks against bad pitching. It was odd seeing Shohei Ohtani available in several leagues, and perhaps fortuitous as he should be activated this week and start a few games. Ohtani was acquired in 26 OCs for an AWB of $17. In Main Events, there were 12 shares available and they went for a reasonable $12 a pop. I scooped up a rare Ohtani share in an OC for $2, winning a tiebreaker over the team in 1st place in that league. Andy Pages will be activated on Tuesday, which should push Tommy Edman back to second base. Pages had been out since August 21, but was producing at an exciting clip before the injury — .272 – 72 R – 21 HR – 80 RBI – 12 SB in 550 PA. Managers who acquired him are hoping that he dusts the cobwebs back off and gets right into the swing of things, with all the marbles on the line.
| # | Player | Team | Position(s) | % of Lgs Added | AWB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Andy Pages | LAD | OF | 60% | $5 |
| 2 | JR Ritchie | ATL | SP | 57% | $3 |
| 3 | Daniel Lynch IV | KC | SP | 57% | $6 |
| 4 | Samad Taylor | SD | OF | 48% | $5 |
| 5 | Jose Siri | LAA | OF | 45% | $4 |
| 6 | Heliot Ramos | NYY | OF | 35% | $7 |
| 7 | Dansby Swanson | CHC | SS | 35% | $8 |
| 8 | Brayan Bello | BOS | SP | 35% | $11 |
| 9 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 32% | $10 |
| 10 | Garrett Whitlock | BOS | RP | 32% | $5 |
| 11 | Pavin Smith | ARI | 1B | 30% | $4 |
| 12 | Anthony Volpe | NYY | SS | 30% | $5 |
AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
Pitchers were the most popular targets, specifically two-steppers, as we chase wins and strikeouts, hoping the Ratio Monster doesn’t eat our leads in ERA and WHIP. JR Ritchie and Daniel Lynch IV were the most added starters who we expect two starts from this week. Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Lynch had served the Royals well as their top southpaw out of the bullpen for most of the season. He moved to the rotation in August and slowly worked his pitch counts upward. Lynch has made it to five innings in each of his last three starts. His latest one (at HOU on September 16) went well — 5 IP – 2 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 3 K. More of that please as he faces the White Sox and Guardians at Kauffman Stadium in the final week. If I could only choose one for the week, it would be Ritchie.
Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Bello had been the worst starter in the game (6.49 ERA, 1.67 WHIP) through June 4, when he was optioned to Triple-A. Since the All-Star break, mostly out of relief and with two starts, the 27-year-old has been shining. Over those 51.1 innings, he is rocking exemplary ratios (2.28 ERA, 1.01 WHIP) and a 17% K-BB% (22.3% K, 5.3% BB). Bello should make a start against the Cubs next Saturday. The Cubs should be settled into a playoff spot by then, so perhaps they give Pete Crow-Armstrong and some of the other regulars that day off. Boston’s closer Aroldis Chapman has been day-to-day with a lat issue, so perhaps the Red sox have him take it easy and provide Whitlock with some save opportunities. Whitlock has a 7-2 record with a 17.5 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and four saves.
Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.
Better late than never for two punchless Padres who have been quite productive and certainly enjoyed their visit to Coors Field in the first half of last week. Dustin Harris ($10 AWB) and Samad Taylor ($5) have been red hot and playing often over the last 10 days. Though he doesn’t have a home run yet, Harris has been quite productive and helpful to early-bird managers: eight runs, 12 runs batted in and three steals, batting .384 with a 166 wRC+ in 40 plate appearances since September 11. He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.

As always, more reliable starting pitcher depth was available in the 12-team OC pool. Cristian Javier, Anthony Kay, Robert Gasser, Lynch, Yusei Kikuchi, and Max Scherzer were the most added pitchers this week. Javier should pitch twice this week and will hope to put his best foot forward (in this case, his right arm) as the Astros fight for the AL West and a playoff spot. Sutter Health Park is not a fun place to pitch, but the A’s lineup is a watered-down version without Brent Rooker, Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, and Jacob Wilson윌슨. Javier’s first start is in Seattle may not be a picnic with gluten-free granola and Pearl Jam on the Discman.
Milwaukee’s Robert Gasser only draws one start (home vs. STL), but is considered a reliable ratios guy who can score a much-needed win for fantasy managers, as the Brewers will certainly be favorites in that matchup. Gasser earned his fifth win on Saturday, throwing seven scoreless innings against the Orioles. White Sox lefty Anthony Kay has good matchups (at KC on Tuesday and vs. COL on Sunday), though that second start could be pulled away from him. The main problems here is that Kay hasn’t made it to the fifth inning in any of his last five starts. I feel much more comfortable with a single start against the Orioles from Max Scherzer than I do a double (at SEA, at ATH) from wily Yusei Kikuchi. Kikuchi has walked 12 batters in his last three starts.

It’s possible that attraction towards Ryan Johnson this weekend relates to dynasty and keeper formats, and not his start in Seattle this week. Johnson has limited run damage over his last nine starts, since August 6, posting a 2.39 ERA, but with an xFIP (5.01) nearly double the mark. Johnson is more of a 4.25-4.50 ERA guy than a sub-3.00 ERA one, as his 90.9% LOB and .229 BABIP portends.
Perhaps a similar mindset applies to folks who scooped up Jack Perkins, who pitched two quality starts on the road against the Rays (6.2 IP – 4 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 8 K) and the Guardians (6 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 0 BB – 4 K), flashing some of his upside and future potential. Perkins has had a difficult season (5.90 ERA, but a 4.16 xFIP, 1.45 WHIP) and will be a tough streamer at home in Sacramento next season, but the strikeouts (25.2%) should always be there.
Andrew Alvarez should have a rotation spot with the Nationals next season. He has been outstanding since the All-Star break, posting a 2.44 ERA (3.30 FIP, 4.02 xFIP) with a 1.10 WHIP and a 22.7% strikeout rate, though he wasn’t able to secure a win in any of those 10 starts. Alvarez won’t be a particularly coveted target in drafts next season, but should have a NFBC ADP somewhere in the 250-325 overall range. He may be a consideration in NL-only keeper leagues with deep benches and five-plus keepers.
Bold Predictions for Week 27
Gavin Williams and Jacob Misiorowski finish the season tied for the MLB lead in strikeouts with 255. Williams punches out 11 and Misiorowski, eight.
JR Ritchie steps up for his two starts and has a Jack Perkins Week 26 type week, helping managers win league titles.
Cade Cavalli twirls a gem in Detroit this week and pulls his 3.02 ERA under 3.00 to end the season. Cavalli will have a top-60 ADP in 2027.
Jo Adell takes advantage of four left-handed starters this week and earns seven RBIs to reach 100, after falling two RBIs short last season.
One of Cristian Javier or Yusei Kikuchi will remind why streaming pitchers in Sutter Health Park, even if part of a two-step, is a mistake.
Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery hit three home runs each this week and the White Sox score the most runs in Week 27.
The Houston Astros win the NL West and knock the Texas Rangers out of playoff contention.
I hope you enjoyed my column this season and that you found it helpful, or at least entertaining and informative. Stay tuned for more from me next week as we hit the offseason streets. Best of luck this final week!
Vlad writes for RotoGraphs and is the head of fantasy baseball content at FTN Fantasy. He is a Tout Wars Expert League champ, member of the CDM Fantasy Sports Hall of Fame and has been nominated for FSWA writing awards six times. Vlad has been playing fantasy baseball since 1995, winning 42 NFBC leagues since 2012 and ranking in the top percentile in NFBC’s Online Championship contest (33% win rate, 52% cash rate; 64 leagues). Much to the chagrin of his colleagues and most baseball aficionados, Vlad is a lifelong Dodgers fan who claims his first gut call at age 9 was Kirk Gibson’s 1988 World Series home run. You can follow him on X and BlueSky @RotoGut.

item.title: [MLB.com] Rays y Yankees se preparan para su serie crucial en el Bronx
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch; Adam Berry
item.description: NUEVA YORK -- Ha parecido inevitable que la lucha por el Este de la Liga Americana se decidiera esta semana en el Bronx. Los Rays han encabezado la división más competitiva de Grandes Ligas durante gran parte de la temporada y no han cedido el primer lugar de la tabla desde que recuperaron la cima el 27 de junio. Pero los Yankees siempre han estado ahí, amenazando y luego retrocediendo. Pero nunca han estado lo suficientemente lejos como para restarle importancia a lo que podría suceder esta sem
item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK -- Ha parecido inevitable que la lucha por el Este de la Liga Americana se decidiera esta semana en el Bronx.
Los Rays han encabezado la división más competitiva de Grandes Ligas durante gran parte de la temporada y no han cedido el primer lugar de la tabla desde que recuperaron la cima el 27 de junio.
Pero los Yankees siempre han estado ahí, amenazando y luego retrocediendo. Pero nunca han estado lo suficientemente lejos como para restarle importancia a lo que podría suceder esta semana.
Pues bien, llegó el momento.
Los Yankees recibirán a los Rays para una serie de cuatro juegos en el Yankee Stadium, comenzando con una doble-cartelera el martes. Gracias a la magnífica estadía de los Rays en casa y a la serie perdida por los Yankees en Phoenix frente a los Diamondbacks, la pregunta ahora es cuánto tiempo más seguirá viva esta lucha.
Los Rays llegaron a Nueva York con 6.0 juegos de ventaja en la división y apenas siete encuentros por disputarse. Una victoria de Tampa Bay eliminará a los Yankees de la lucha por la División Este y los dejará asegurados en un puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana. Entonces, para que los Yankees tengan alguna posibilidad, deberán completar una barrida de cuatro partidos en tres días.
¿Lo que está en juego? Como dijo una vez Gerrit Cole: “Es mucho”. Entremos en materia.
¿Qué está en juego?
Rays: Ganar apenas un juego les garantizará a los Rays su primer campeonato del Este de la Liga Americana desde el 2021, otorgándoles un pase directo a la Serie Divisional y la ventaja de localía tanto en esa ronda como, si avanzan, en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana. También necesitan una sola victoria para asegurar la serie particular contra los Yankees.
Yankees: El piloto Aaron Boone reconoce que será una “tarea muy difícil” evitar que los Rays celebren con champaña en el Bronx, pero eso es exactamente lo que pretenden hacer. Empezaron la temporada buscando cambiar la narrativa, después de quedarse cortos ante los Azulejos el año pasado. En cambio, están a punto de tener que conformarse nuevamente con un premio de consolación y verse obligados a ganar una serie al mejor de tres juegos.
¿Cómo están alineadas las rotaciones?
Rays: Enviarán a sus mejores dos abridores al montículo para la doble-cartelera del martes. Primero será el derecho veterano Nick Martínez, líder del clubhouse y su fuente más confiable de innings. Tampa Bay tiene marca de 22-7 esta temporada en los juegos iniciados por el cubano-estadounidense. Después, le tocará a Drew Rasmussen, uno de los mejores abridores de la Liga Americana. Los Rays no han perdido una apertura de Rasmussen desde el 9 de julio, con marca perfecta de 11-0 en sus presentaciones desde entonces. Martínez lanzará con un día adicional de descanso, mientras que Rasmussen trabajará con cuatro días de descanso apenas por séptima vez esta campaña. El zurdo Ian Seymour y el derecho dominicano Freddy Peralta estarían alineados para abrir el miércoles y el jueves, respectivamente.
Yankees: Carlos Rodón y Max Fried abrirán los juegos de la doble-cartelera, en ese orden. Ambos han lidiado con lesiones esta temporada, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado. En tres aperturas de septiembre, Rodón tiene marca de 2-0 con efectividad de 2.08, dejando atrás un episodio de inflamación en el codo izquierdo. Después de ingresar dos veces a la lista de lesionados por una contusión ósea en el codo de lanzar, Fried tiene récord de 1-0 y promedio de carreras limpias de 1.69 en tres aperturas este mes. Cole y Cam Schlittler, favorito para ganar el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, seguirán en el tercer y cuarto partidos de la serie, respectivamente.
¿Qué ha estado funcionando bien últimamente para cada equipo?
Rays: ¿Todo? Los Rays acaban de registrar récord de 8-1 durante su última estadía en casa de la campaña regular y han ganado cuatro series consecutivas contra los Bravos, Astros, Atléticos y Medias Rojas. Desde que fueron barridos en una serie de cuatro partidos en el Fenway Park tras la pausa del Juego de Estrellas, tienen marca de 39-18, la mejor de la Gran Carpa desde el 20 de julio. Su pitcheo abridor se ha visto particularmente sólido, con efectividad de 2.81 este mes, sólo detrás de la de los Yankees. Como de costumbre, han encontrado distintas maneras de anotar carreras, incluyendo ataques tempraneros como el del domingo y un par de jonrones para dejar en el terreno al rival por parte del candidato al JMV de la Liga Americana, el dominicano Junior Caminero.
Yankees: De repente, estos Yankees se encuentran apoyándose en la fortaleza de su pitcheo, confiando en que la ofensiva terminará respondiendo. Ben Rice conectó su 39no cuadrangular, la mayor cantidad del equipo, cumpliendo una predicción que Boone hizo durante los Entrenamientos de Primavera. Rice dijo que Boone estaba bromeando con él, quedándose con “uno o dos” por debajo de la cifra que él prefería, así que habrá que estar atentos a Rice mientras busca su 40mo vuelacercas esta semana. Austin Wells ha conectado tres bambinazos en sus últimos seis encuentros, mientras que el puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos ha volado la cerca en sus últimos dos partidos. Podría ser una pieza importante si los Yankees quieren hacerse sentir en octubre.
¿Cuáles son algunas áreas de preocupación que podrían convertirse en un problema esta semana o en la postemporada?
Rays: Muchos jugadores de los Rays han dado un paso al frente, pero el primer bate del equipo, el cubano Yandy Díaz, ha tenido un mes complicado, con línea ofensiva de .229/.286/.357 en septiembre. Él marca la pauta para la alineación, así que obviamente será importante que llegue en su mejor nivel a octubre. Y esto es realmente buscarle la quinta pata al gato, considerando que tiene marca de 3-0 con un salvamento y efectividad de 1.42 este mes, pero Bryan Baker, líder de Grandes Ligas en salvamentos, suma más bases por bolas (cuatro) que ponches (dos) en siete presentaciones durante septiembre. También necesitarán que sea dominante en la postemporada.
Yankees: Más allá del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha de Aaron Judge, un asunto que los Yankees están manejando como si fuera un secreto del estado, comienzan a surgir preocupaciones sobre el estado del bullpen. La velocidad de Brent Headrick ha disminuido y el relevista podría estar mostrando señales de fatiga después de liderar las Mayores con 79 presentaciones. Tim Hill no ha sido la máquina automática de provocar rodados de años anteriores. Michael Fulmer permitió un jonrón que decidió un juego en Arizona. Pero no hay un asunto más importante que demostrar que pueden ganar sin Judge, el motor alrededor del cual gira su ofensiva. Tienen marca de 48-41 sin él, comparada con 41-25 cuando ha estado en acción.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Postemporada MLB: clasificaciones, salud de Ohtani y Judge y premios
item.dc:creator: DAVID BRANDT
item.description: Postemporada MLB: clasificaciones, salud de Ohtani y Judge y premios La postemporada de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol se acerca rápidamente, con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en busca de un tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial. Sin embargo, aún está por verse cuánto podrán participar algunas de las mayores estrellas del deporte cuando llegue octubre. item.content:encoded:
Postemporada MLB: clasificaciones, salud de Ohtani y Judge y premios
La postemporada de las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol se acerca rápidamente, con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles en busca de un tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial. Sin embargo, aún está por verse cuánto podrán participar algunas de las mayores estrellas del deporte cuando llegue octubre.
Los Dodgers vuelven a estar entre los mejores equipos de las Grandes Ligas, y tendrán varios retadores en octubre, incluidos los Cerveceros de Milwaukee y los Rays de Tampa Bay. Los tres equipos podrían terminar la temporada regular con 100 victorias o más. Los Ángeles está ahí pese a que la salud del cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso Shohei Ohtani es motivo de preocupación.
Los Yankees de Nueva York, los Medias Rojas de Boston y los Bravos de Atlanta también han asegurado lugares en la postemporada. El tres veces Jugador Más Valioso de los Yankees, Aaron Judge, lidia con una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha que lo mantendrá en la lista de lesionados al menos hasta el último día de la temporada regular.
La temporada regular termina este domingo y, aunque el cuadro de playoffs de 12 equipos parece estar mayormente definido, hay algunos aspirantes con pocas probabilidades de llegar a la postemporada, y los enfrentamientos específicos están en movimiento.
A continuación, algunas de las cosas a seguir mientras la temporada llega a su fin.
Equipos que pueden asegurar un puesto de playoffs el lunes
Ningún equipo puede asegurar un puesto de playoffs el lunes, ya que la mayor parte de la liga tendrá el día libre.
Hay un partido importante en la Liga Americana, donde los Azulejos de Toronto viajan para enfrentar a los Orioles de Baltimore. Los Azulejos se mantienen apenas en el borde de la pelea en la LA, al iniciar el día a tres juegos del último puesto de comodín.
Lucha en la Liga Americana sigue en duda mientras la Liga Nacional está más definida
Esta temporada ha habido bastante mediocridad en las divisiones Central y Oeste de la LA, lo que ha derivado en carreras por el banderín fascinantes y podría llevar a que un equipo con marca por debajo de .500 llegue a la postemporada.
Los Guardianes de Cleveland (81-75) tienen una ligera ventaja sobre los Medias Blancas de Chicago (80-76) en la Central de la LA, mientras que los Rangers de Texas (78-78) están apenas por delante de los Astros de Houston (77-79) en el Oeste de la LA.
En la Liga Nacional, el cuadro de playoffs está casi definido.
Los Cachorros de Chicago (87-69), Padres de San Diego (87-69) y Filis de Filadelfia (86-70) se disputan posiciones en la carrera por el comodín, pero casi con seguridad llegarán a la postemporada. El único equipo a una distancia relativamente cercana es el de los Diamondbacks de Arizona (82-74), que está a cuatro juegos.
Carreras por el MVP, estadísticas a seguir
Los principales premios de la MLB probablemente no tendrán mucho drama esta temporada.
Ambas carreras por el MVP tienen claros favoritos, con Pete Crow-Armstrong, de Chicago, despegándose rumbo al honor en la LN, mientras que el cubano Yordan Alvarez, de Houston, es la opción probable en la LA, aunque el dominicano Junior Caminero, de Tampa Bay, también ha tenido una temporada fantástica. Alvarez aún tiene una oportunidad de lograr la rara Triple Corona. Lidera la LA en promedio de bateo con .313, pero sus 40 jonrones están a uno de Caminero y sus 99 carreras impulsadas están a seis de las de Pete Alonso, de Baltimore.
Para el premio Cy Young, el lanzallamas de Milwaukee Jacob Misiorowski y el as de Nueva York Cam Schlittler son los favoritos en la LN y la LA, respectivamente.
Las carreras por el Novato del Año también parecen definidas, con Sal Stewart, de Cincinnati, y su temporada de 110 carreras impulsadas como líder en la LN, y Kevin McGonigle, de Detroit, como favorito en la LA.
¿Cuál es el formato de playoffs de la MLB?
Hay 12 equipos que clasifican a la postemporada de la MLB, incluidos seis equipos tanto de la LA como de la LN. Los tres ganadores de división en cada liga reciben las siembras número 1 a número 3, ordenadas por récord de victorias y derrotas. Luego, los tres equipos de comodín reciben las siembras número 4 a número 6, también ordenadas por récord de victorias y derrotas.
Los dos mejores equipos con el mejor récord tanto en la LA como en la LN avanzan automáticamente a la Serie Divisional. Los otros ocho equipos juegan la Serie de Comodines, que es un formato al mejor de tres y comienza el martes 30 de septiembre. Tanto en la LA como en la LN, el sembrado número 6 viajará para enfrentar al sembrado número 3, mientras que el sembrado número 5 va contra el número 4. El sembrado más alto es anfitrión de los tres juegos.
Los ganadores avanzan luego a la Serie Divisional al mejor de cinco, seguida por la Serie de Campeonato de Liga al mejor de siete y una Serie Mundial al mejor de siete entre los ganadores de la LA y la LN.
¿Cuál es el calendario de la postemporada de la MLB?
Ronda de Comodines: 29 de septiembre-1 de octubre (NBC/Peacock)
Serie Divisional: 3-10 de octubre (LA en TBS, LN en FOX/FS1)
Serie de Campeonato: 11-20 de octubre (LA en TBS, LN en FOX/FS1)
Serie Mundial: 23-31 de octubre (FOX)
¿Quiénes son los favoritos para ganar la Serie Mundial?
Los Dodgers (+220) son los favoritos para conquistar un tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial, mientras que los Cerveceros (+600), Yankees (+800) y Rays (+800) son considerados los principales contendientes.
___

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Yankees' rotation vs. Rays is setting up a potential Wild Card Series mistake
item.dc:creator: Adam Weinrib
item.description: The New York Yankees are almost guaranteed to face the Boston Red Sox in an upcoming best-of-three Wild Card series, and can lock up homefield advantage with either a singular win in their final seven games or one Boston loss. That makes every rotation decision or perceive
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are almost guaranteed to face the Boston Red Sox in an upcoming best-of-three Wild Card series, and can lock up homefield advantage with either a singular win in their final seven games or one Boston loss. The time is now for forecasting and getting your ducks in a row, and the Yankees have acknowledged as such; resetting Brent Headrick, for example, is more important than going all out to embarrass the Tampa Bay Rays this week.
That makes every rotation decision or perceived pattern seem magnified, especially after Boston lined up their starters for their upcoming series with the Cleveland Guardians: Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, Ranger Suárez. Is that the chips falling where they may, or is that foreshadowing? Either way, while winking and nodding, it's probably time to read similarly into the way the Yankees are handlng things.
That's why our eyebrows raised on Sunday when the Yanks revealed that Cam Schlittler and Gerrit Cole will stay on turn in the Rays series (for now), with Schlittler closing the four-game set and Cole pitching Game 3, both staying out of the doubleheader. That will leave Cole with an extra day of rest ahead of the WIld Card opener and Schlittler on normal rest. You're not saying ... ?
All the love in the world to Gerrit Cole, who got closer to securing an all-important Wild Card Series start with his strong appearance in the desert on Friday night. But given that his spot in the rotation in general has been rightly questioned, there is no world where he should start Game 1 over Schlittler. That is not even something that should be rolling around in the canals of my addled gray brain. And yet!
Yankees giving Gerrit Cole the rest he needs ahead of Wild Card Series. Will Cam Schlittler even start vs. Rays?
For now, this is all hypothetical, but ... Cole has always seemed like a candidate for a deciding Game 3, but nothing before it. Would the Yankees really dare to use him in a deciding game with three extra days of rest building up on his right arm?
And, if the Rays clinch the AL East this week and the Yankees lock down their positioning, will they use Schlittler at all in this series? Will he make a perfunctory three-inning cameo just to keep his sea legs ahead of the Sox showdown and prevent overthrowing/overcompensating? The Cy Young race between he and Dylan Cease is informally over, and Cease may not even be healthy enough to make another start. If positioning gets more solidified throughout the week, these decisions only become more fascinating.
As of now, though, before any adjustments ... it seems like there's at least a chance the Yankees are lining up Cole for Game 1 - or working him out of the picture entirely.

item.title: [tsn.ca] The latest on MLB postseason clinches, Ohtani and Judge health updates, awards races and more
